claims.text: The target material family is multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys, and the primary mechanical property of interest is tensile ductility during aging.
RHEAs containing specific D0a or D022 chemical ordering will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The proposed non-monotonic ductility transition occurs near the order-disorder transition temperature and is driven by SRO evolution and precipitate coherency.
The W-Ta-Ni-Fe-based example has a dual BCC/FCC microstructure.
The Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti-based example contains BCC/FCC or BCC/B2 phases.
The initial solutionized or as-cast alloy contains incipient or short-range chemical ordering.
Stepwise aging between 600 and 900 °C can induce nucleation and growth of coherent δ-lamellae or γ″ precipitates.
Continued aging in the proposed temperature range will eventually disorder or dissolve the coherent precipitates.
The relevant aging experiments should be conducted in argon or vacuum.
Tensile strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-3 s^-1 are relevant boundary conditions.
A disordered matrix with limited SRO permits relatively unrestricted dislocation glide and therefore an initially ductile state.
Coherent δ-lamellae or γ″ precipitates produce hardening and restrict dislocation motion.
Restricted dislocation motion creates interfacial stress concentrations and premature cracks that reduce ductility.
Disordering or extensive coarsening near or above the ODTT reduces lattice misfit and order hardening, restores dislocation mobility, and recovers ductility.
Ductility will be high initially, reach a sharp minimum at intermediate aging conditions, and recover at longer aging times or higher temperatures.
Comparable multiphase alloys without an ODTT near the aging temperature generally show only monotonic softening or monotonic embrittlement.
The transition is bounded by the alloy-specific ODTT, which is suggested to be close to the irradiation temperature in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEAs.
A critical ordered-phase volume fraction is required to generate order hardening without immediate fracture.
Composition-dependent differences in SRO decay and precipitate coarsening kinetics may mask the proposed non-monotonic behavior.
A monotonic ductility curve, or a ductility minimum that does not coincide with peak SRO or peak coherent-precipitate volume fraction, is defined as a falsifying outcome.
